title: self-update fails on a platform-incomplete latest release instead of falling back to the newest release with a matching asset
description:
Self-update fails outright when the newest release has no asset for the running platform, instead of falling back to the newest release that does. A node can be blocked from updating at all while a perfectly good build sits one tag back.

Observed on helsinki, 2026-07-30T09:17Z:

    cara self-update run
    cara self_update_failed: release v0.0.42 has no asset cara-0.0.42-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
    (available: ["cara-0.0.42-aarch64-darwin.sha256", "cara-0.0.42-aarch64-darwin.tar.gz"])

Release inventory at that moment:

    v0.0.42   2026-07-30T07:57Z   darwin only  <- latest, no linux asset
    v0.0.41   2026-07-30T07:27Z   HAS linux
    v0.0.40   2026-07-30T06:45Z   HAS linux
    v0.0.39   2026-07-30T05:56Z   HAS linux

So helsinki was not blocked by a broken build. It was blocked by a policy of only ever considering the newest tag. A usable Linux binary existed 30 minutes older and was ignored.

WHY THIS IS NOT A RARE EDGE CASE

Multi-platform releases do not publish atomically. Per-platform jobs finish at different times, and some fail or get starved independently: on this fleet, aarch64-linux jobs have been observed starved on a permanently busy runner (bd-893ff0), and a separate defect fails an aarch64-linux release job after the binary has already published (bd-8b49a7). Caravan cut five releases in two hours on the day this was observed. With that cadence, the window where "latest" is platform-incomplete is not an anomaly; it is a routine state, and every Linux node hits it.

The failure is also worst where it matters most. Whichever platform is slowest or flakiest to build is exactly the platform whose nodes can never self-update, because "latest" is perpetually ahead of their last usable asset.

WANTED

Resolve self-update against "the newest release carrying an asset for THIS platform", not "the newest release". Concretely:

- Walk releases newest-first and select the first one with a matching asset, within a bounded lookback.
- Report the choice explicitly: "updating to v0.0.41 (v0.0.42 has no x86_64-linux asset)". Silently taking an older version would be its own problem; the point is to proceed while saying why.
- Keep a bounded search. If no release within, say, the last N carries a matching asset, that IS a real failure and should say so - the platform's build pipeline is broken, which is a different and more serious condition than one late tag.
- Consider whether a release that is platform-incomplete should be marked as such, so consumers can distinguish "still publishing" from "this platform failed".

This belongs in the shared updatable-cli behaviour rather than in cara specifically, since any tool using it has the same exposure.

IMPACT IS LARGER THAN A VERSION LAG. THIS BUG IS CURRENTLY KEEPING A MERGE QUEUE BROKEN.

Measured on helsinki, 2026-07-30 ~11:45Z:

    which cara            /home/harry/.local/bin/cara   (a real binary, exactly what self-update maintains)
    cara --version        0.0.27

The caravan fixes that make the queue function are in v0.0.30/31 - notably a producer/consumer problem-kind mismatch that left the head-of-line guard silently dead since 0.0.27, with all tests green because the unit test injected the old kind by hand.

So helsinki is running the LAST version before the fix, and self-update cannot advance it because the newest release is platform-incomplete for x86_64-linux.

THE CAUSAL CHAIN, END TO END:

    self-update refuses to fall back to the newest release WITH a linux asset
      -> helsinki stays on cara 0.0.27
      -> 0.0.27 predates the head-of-line fix
      -> the merge queue cannot function correctly on the node that hosts it
      -> no caravan forms

Context on how much this cost: a caravan had never once formed on cacophony until 2026-07-30, and days of correct diagnosis by three separate agents went into code nobody was running (bd-ee4a2d). When one finally formed, it was against a runtime built ad-hoc for verification rather than the installed binary.

Right now there are two CLEAN candidate PRs on cacophony and no caravan, on a node whose cara predates the fix.

That reframes the priority. This is not "a node is one version behind". It is "the node that hosts the merge queue cannot run a working merge queue, and the mechanism that would fix it refuses to act because an unrelated platform's build was late".

Note also the compounding property already recorded on this bead: whichever platform is slowest or flakiest to build is exactly the platform whose nodes can never self-update. helsinki is x86_64-linux, and x86_64-linux is the platform observed being starved on a permanently busy runner (bd-893ff0) and failing a release job after the binary already published (bd-8b49a7).

title: Add integration test for updatable-cli promote_next / maybe_apply_staged_update
description: promote_next and maybe_apply_staged_update perform the on-disk rename/re-exec promotion contract (the riskiest part touching real binaries), but src/lib.rs only tests current_status. A tempdir-based test that stages a fake <tool>_next, calls promote_next, and asserts the installed binary appears with 0755 perms (and that promote_next returns None when nothing is staged) would lock in the promotion semantics. Filed via reflect-session/cacophony-bead-scope from updatable-cli scaffold review (no active bead; queue empty).
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Have register_update_tool publish MCP output schemas
description: Discovered during Caravan bd-af5c3d SPEC/CLI/MCP parity audit: updatable-cli's UpdateStatus, LatestReleaseInfo, and UpdateOutcome already derive JsonSchema, but register_update_tool uses add_typed_tool rather than add_typed_tool_with_output_schema. Consequently self_update_status/check/run metadata omit outputSchema and hosts must duplicate the registrar to satisfy a fully typed MCP contract. Switch the registrar and add metadata tests; preserve names and handlers.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-1

title: Install a downloaded release to an explicit target directory
description:
Today the updater only replaces the currently running executable in place. That leaves consumers with no first-party option when the running binary is immutable or package-managed, for example /nix/store/...-caravan-0.0.7/bin/cara, where an in-place write is impossible and would corrupt the store closure if it somehow succeeded.

Add a generic capability: resolve and download the selected release asset, verify its digest, and install it to an explicit caller-supplied target directory instead of over the current executable. Preserve every existing check (version resolution, asset selection, digest verification, executable permissions, atomic replace within the target directory).

Deliberate scope boundary: this crate must NOT decide where installing is acceptable. It performs no package-manager detection, no PATH-precedence policy, and no store protection. It takes an explicit destination and reports exactly what it wrote, including resolved source asset, version, destination path, and artifact hash. Callers own policy.

Consumer counterpart is a Caravan bead that adds the forced self-update path: it refuses store and Homebrew destinations outright, requires the destination to precede the package-managed binary in PATH, and emits a loud shadowing receipt. File that Caravan bead as the dependent so ordering is explicit.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: Make updatable-cli compile and stage safely on Windows
description:
Ring's native Windows MIDI/Ableton build is blocked because updatable-cli is explicitly Unix-only: it uses std::os::unix PermissionsExt/CommandExt, assumes binaries named without `.exe`, and release_target only maps linux/darwin. Ring imports Updater types across main/update/MCP/TUI, so target-gating one call is insufficient.

Add Windows portability without weakening Unix behavior:
- Compile the full crate/tests for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.
- cfg-gate executable permissions and exec replacement; preserve current atomic staged-update behavior on Unix.
- Define safe Windows staged/current executable naming (`tool.exe`, `tool_next.exe`) and a promotion strategy compatible with Windows locking. If replacing a running exe cannot be made safe in this slice, make startup promotion an explicit nonfatal/no-op with actionable status rather than failing compilation or corrupting the current binary.
- Extend release_target / Tendril-style asset naming with a documented canonical Windows suffix (coordinate with ring's planned `x86_64-windows` asset).
- Keep Updater, MCP registration, current_status, check_latest, and download/checksum APIs usable by Windows callers.
- Add cfg-specific unit tests and a Windows CI compile/test job on an existing self-hosted Windows runner if the project has one.
- Document host integration expectations for downstream CLIs.

Downstream: ring-mods bd-af3e23 needs this on main to ship a native Windows Ring MIDI bridge for Harry's Ableton Live test.
creator: aurora:ring-mods:aurora-ring-mods-ring-dev-aur-0

title: Rework CI to use a Nix devshell for the toolchain (azure-ephemeral runners)
description:
Operator directive (2026-06-28): the azure-ephemeral runners are Nix-based, so prebuilt-toolchain actions (dtolnay/rust-toolchain downloads a rustc that won't run under NixOS's linker) fail with "missing toolchain". Rework CI to obtain the toolchain from a Nix devshell instead of a runner image / rustup download.

updatable-cli has no flake today. Add a minimal flake.nix exposing a default devShell with the Rust toolchain (cargo, rustc, rustfmt, clippy) — the crate is pure-Rust (rustls TLS, miniz flate2), so no system libs needed. Rework .github/workflows/ci.yml: drop the dtolnay/rust-toolchain step and run each check via `nix develop --command cargo ...` (runners have Nix+flakes preinstalled). Keep checkout + cargo cache.

Acceptance: flake.nix + flake.lock committed; `nix develop --command cargo fmt --all --check / clippy --all-targets -D warnings / test` all pass locally; ci.yml uses nix develop. Note: updatable-cli still needs adding to the runner pool `repos` allowlist (separate operator action) before CI actually runs there.
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Add mock-HTTP tests for updatable-cli check_latest/stage_next happy path
description: The core download/verify/stage flow (Updater::check_latest, stage_next, verify_sha256 against a real release shape) has no test coverage; only release_target, sha256 verify, and current_status are tested in src/lib.rs. A mockito/httpmock-backed test serving a fake releases/latest JSON plus a tarball+sha256 asset would harden the riskiest network path. Filed via reflect-session/cacophony-bead-scope from updatable-cli scaffold review (no active bead; queue empty).

title: Document all public items and enforce with #![warn(missing_docs)]
description:
A `RUSTFLAGS="-W missing_docs" cargo build` shows 39 undocumented public items in src/lib.rs (7 structs, 22 struct fields, 8 methods, 2 associated functions), including the public result types (UpdateStatus, LatestReleaseInfo, UpdateOutcome, AssetNames) and several Updater methods (new, config, current_status, check_latest, stage_next, run_update) and EmptyArgs/UpdateError. For a crate that ships full crates.io publishing metadata, this leaves a sparse docs.rs page.

Add `#![warn(missing_docs)]` at the crate root and write a concise doc comment for every public item so the lint is satisfied. Because CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, this also enforces documentation on all future public items (new undocumented pub items will fail CI).

Acceptance: `RUSTFLAGS="-W missing_docs" cargo build` is clean (0 missing-doc warnings); cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings + test (22 unit + 2 doc-tests) stay green; cargo doc --no-deps builds clean. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Add CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog) for the publish-intended crate
description:
updatable-cli ships with full crates.io publishing metadata (description, license, keywords, categories, repository, homepage) but has no CHANGELOG.md. For a reusable crate intended to be embedded across the CLI suite, a changelog is standard, expected documentation so adopters can see what changed between versions.

State: version 0.1.0, no git tags, no GitHub releases (pre-first-release), so all current work belongs under an Unreleased / 0.1.0 section.

Add a CHANGELOG.md following the Keep a Changelog convention with an Unreleased (toward 0.1.0) section summarizing the implemented surface, grouped Added/Changed:
- Updater core: current_status, check_latest, stage_next (sha256-verified), promote_next, run_update; maybe_apply_staged_update re-exec; register_update_tool MCP surface (self_update_status/check/run); Tendril-style asset strategy + Custom; release_target.
- Private-repo support: github_token, gh_account / gh_token_fallback, bearer dropped on cross-host redirect (bd-d3e3c8).
- Repo hygiene + CI workflow (bd-c381de); mock-HTTP + integration tests (bd-378b81, bd-247d71).
- Unix-only support made explicit; dead non-unix branch removed (bd-3b5d1c).
- Friendlier check_latest errors for 404 no-releases and 403/429 rate-limit (bd-d7a396).

Acceptance: CHANGELOG.md present, accurate, Keep-a-Changelog format; cargo fmt/clippy/test still green (docs-only, no code impact). Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: Make Unix-only platform support explicit; remove dead #[cfg(not(unix))] exec_replace branch
description:
Portability inconsistency in src/lib.rs.

Current state:
- Module unconditionally does `use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;` (top of lib.rs) and calls `set_mode(...)` in `set_executable` and tests. These are Unix-only APIs; `std::os::unix` does not exist on Windows, so the crate cannot compile on non-Unix targets.
- `release_target()` only maps linux->linux and macos->darwin, and bails on any other OS. So even at runtime only Linux/macOS are supported.
- Despite that, `exec_replace` has a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` fallback (spawn + exit) alongside the `#[cfg(unix)]` `CommandExt::exec` path. Because the unconditional unix import already prevents non-unix compilation, the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` branch is unreachable/dead code and never builds.

Net: the crate is effectively Unix-only (Linux/macOS), but the dead non-unix branch and the cfg gating imply cross-platform intent that does not hold. For a reusable crate published with full crates.io metadata, this is misleading.

Recommended minimal fix (commit to Unix-only honestly):
- Remove the dead `#[cfg(not(unix))]` exec_replace fn and the now-redundant `#[cfg(unix)]` gate on the remaining definition, making exec_replace a plain Unix fn consistent with the rest of the module.
- Add an explicit "Platform support: Unix (Linux/macOS) only" note to the crate-level doc comment and the README.

Optional larger follow-up (defer unless there is demand): add real Windows support — cfg-gate the unix imports, provide a Windows set_executable no-op, and add a Windows release_target arm plus a zip-based asset strategy. Not in scope for this bead.

Acceptance: crate still builds + cargo test/clippy/fmt pass; no dead non-unix branch remains; docs/README state Unix-only support. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli (board was empty).
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Rollback support: keep <tool>_prev and auto-restore on bad update
description: Idea (drafted while idle): rollback safety for self-update. On promote_next, keep the outgoing binary as <tool>_prev; add Updater::rollback() to restore it. Also make maybe_apply_staged_update auto-rollback to <tool>_prev if the freshly promoted binary fails to re-exec / exits nonzero immediately, so a bad release can't brick the tool. Pure-Unix, testable. Complements the existing atomic promote.

title: Authenticate private GitHub release asset downloads through API
description: Caravan v0.0.1 private-repository live self-update proof: release metadata succeeds with gh-token fallback, but run then downloads `browser_download_url` at `https://github.com/harryaskham/caravan/releases/download/v0.0.1/cara-0.0.1-aarch64-darwin.tar.gz` and receives HTTP 404 even with GH_TOKEN. Exact 0.0.0 fixture binary, temp HOME, published assets/checksums; metadata/check is green. GitHub private assets require authenticated `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/assets/{asset_id}` with `Accept: application/octet-stream`, following the signed redirect without forwarding Authorization cross-origin. Preserve public browser URL behavior, checksum verification, token secrecy, and redirect auth stripping. Add mock tests for private API asset IDs, 302 signed redirects, public assets, missing token 404 guidance, and checksum leg. Caravan bd-0ae65f remains blocked on live `self-update run` until a pinned updatable-cli fix lands.

title: [operator-action] Add updatable-cli to azure-ephemeral runner pool repos allowlist
description:
updatable-cli's CI is fully migrated to the azure-ephemeral runners (runs-on [self-hosted, azure-ephemeral] + Nix devshell toolchain, validated locally, landed 2ec7001), but updatable-cli is NOT in the runner pool's repos allowlist — so its CI jobs queue indefinitely with no runner (verified: pushes 28330594095, 28334705783 stuck queued 3-4h+). Per the directive, only x86/Linux pure build/test (no secrets/tailnet), so once added it runs clean.

OPERATOR ACTION: append `updatable-cli` to `repos` in sandbox/ops/terraform/runners.nix (cacophony/collective repo) and redeploy. This is outside updatable-cli worker scope. Pool currently covers: collective, cacophony, agent-utils, android-utils, apple-utils, tendril, omni-cli, ring-mods, kittui, midi2hid — not updatable-cli. Tracking the remaining gate so it isn't lost in chat.

UPDATE (2026-07-01, per bd-f35766 deploy broadcast): the azure-ephemeral runner pool now has a shared Azure Files build-cache at /mnt/build-cache (shared CARGO_HOME + per-runner scratch, cleaned on exit); all 11 runners intact. DEPLOY-PATH CLARIFICATION for this operator-action: sandbox CI workflows (sandbox-terraform.yml, runner-image.yml) have NO Azure OIDC federation and fail at Azure Login; sandbox-terraform.yml is now plan-only. So after appending updatable-cli to repos in sandbox/ops/terraform/runners.nix, the redeploy must be applied MANUALLY via sandbox/deploy.sh (local az + real secrets), NOT by pushing and expecting CI to apply it. Still operator/ops scope; noting the corrected apply path so the allowlist change is not pushed-and-forgotten. Caveat: SMB build-cache does not host /nix, so it does not fix nix-build OOM (bd-256755 tracks binary-cache substitution); updatable-cli CI is pure x86 build/test per the migration, so this cache is a net win for it.

CLARIFICATION (2026-07-02, re bd-f35766 fleet CI regression): the SMB-CARGO_HOME rustup-hardlink failure breaking azure rust repos does NOT affect updatable-cli. Verified in this checkout: ci.yml provisions the toolchain via `nix develop --command cargo ...` from the flake devShells.default (nixpkgs cargo+rustc), NOT dtolnay/rust-toolchain+rustup, so there is no rustup toolchain-install that would hardlink into /mnt/build-cache/cargo-home. The workflow also caches default ~/.cargo via actions/cache and references neither /mnt/build-cache nor CARGO_HOME. Net: this regression is NOT a reason to defer the runner-allowlist gate for updatable-cli — its CI is immune by construction. (Supersedes the earlier "net win" phrasing: accurate statement is "immune to the rustup-link breakage; toolchain is nixpkgs via devshell".)
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Add a compile-checked rustdoc example for the MCP register_update_tool surface
description:
The crate's headline feature is the MCP integration (register_update_tool exposing self_update_status/check/run "for free"), but there is no compile-checked example of it — the README's MCP block is marked `rust,ignore` with placeholder types, so it never compiles, and the new crate-level Example only covers current_status.

Add a second crate-level rustdoc example (a real runnable doc-test, no network/IO) demonstrating the MCP surface:

- ToolRouter::<Ctx>::new()
- register_update_tool(&mut router, |_ctx| UpdaterConfig::new(tool, version, repo))
- assert the three tool names are registered via router.tool_metadata()

This mirrors the existing register_update_tool_registers_the_three_self_update_tools unit test but as documentation, so the primary public MCP entry point gains a compile- and run-checked example. mcp_cli is a normal dependency so it is available to doc-tests (same as anyhow in the current_status example).

Acceptance: cargo test runs the new doc-test (now 2 doc-tests) and it passes; fmt + clippy + the 22 unit tests stay green. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: Optional release signature verification (minisign/cosign/GPG) for downloaded binaries
description: Idea (drafted while idle): add release signature verification beyond the sha256 checksum. A self-updater that fetches+executes binaries is a supply-chain target; sha256 only proves integrity vs the published checksum, not authenticity. Add optional minisign/cosign/GPG signature verification of the release asset against a configured public key, gated by a verify policy in UpdaterConfig. Default off (back-compat), opt-in via with_signing_key(...). High value, self-contained, testable with mock keys. Sister to existing sha256 verify in stage_next.
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Crate is not crates.io-publishable: mcp-cli git dependency has no version (cargo publish fails)
description:
updatable-cli ships full crates.io publishing metadata (description, license, keywords, categories, repository, homepage, readme) implying it is meant to be published, but `cargo publish --dry-run` FAILS:

  error: failed to verify manifest ... all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when publishing. dependency `mcp-cli` does not specify a version

Root cause: Cargo.toml depends on `mcp-cli = { git = "https://github.com/harryaskham/mcp-cli", branch = "main" }`. crates.io rejects git/path-only dependencies; every dependency (including optional ones) must carry a semver version that exists on crates.io.

Important: feature-gating / making mcp-cli optional does NOT bypass this — optional dependencies still require a version requirement at publish time. So the crate cannot be published to crates.io until mcp-cli itself is published to crates.io.

Options considered:
1. Publish mcp-cli to crates.io, then in updatable-cli pin a version (git for dev via [patch]).
2. Decide updatable-cli is intentionally NOT crates.io-published (git-only) and relax the publishing metadata.
3. Split the MCP surface into a separate crate so the core can publish without mcp-cli.

Verified via `cargo publish --dry-run`. Discovered during overnight in-lane review (node aurora).

DECISION (2026-06-23, operator via choice-019ef688, freeform "no crates.io, just idle"): option 2 — updatable-cli is intentionally NOT published to crates.io; it is consumed git-only across the CLI suite. The "not publishable" state is BY DESIGN, not a defect, so no fix is required. Optional non-urgent follow-up if ever desired: relax the crates.io publishing metadata (keywords/categories) so it doesn't imply crates.io intent. Deferred per operator "just idle"; left as draft for the operator to discard or action at leisure.
creator: aurora:updatable-cli:aurora-updatable-cli-updatable-cli-dev-aur-0

title: Repo hygiene: apply rustfmt, fix clippy derivable_impls, add CI workflow
description:
The crate builds and all 16 tests pass, but routine hygiene has drifted:

- `cargo fmt --check` reports formatting diffs across ~21 regions of src/lib.rs.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` emits one warning: `AssetStrategy`'s manual `impl Default` can be derived (clippy::derivable_impls) — replace with `#[derive(Default)]` + `#[default]` on the `TendrilStyle` variant.
- There is no `.github/workflows` CI to guard fmt/clippy/test on push, even though this crate is intended to be published and consumed by other repos.

Scope: apply rustfmt, fix the clippy lint, and add a minimal GitHub Actions workflow running fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, and cargo test. No behavioural changes. Filed from updatable-cli dev session on operator 'continue'.

title: Private-repo support: attach token to asset downloads + optional gh-account token source
description:
Private-repo updates are only half-wired today. `UpdaterConfig.github_token` is sent as Authorization: Bearer only on the check_latest metadata request (lib.rs:224); the actual asset/checksum downloads in stage_next go through download_bytes/download_text which set User-Agent only and never attach the token. So even a correctly-authed caller cannot download a private release asset — it 404s. Confirmed bug, not caller misuse (kittui is wiring a stopgap).

Scope:
1. Thread the resolved token into asset + checksum downloads with redirect-safe handling that strips Authorization on cross-host redirects (GitHub -> signed S3 URL) so private downloads actually work.
2. Add an opt-in convenience for callers to source a token from the local gh CLI when none is set explicitly: new UpdaterConfig fields gh_account (Option<String>) and gh_token_fallback (bool), plus a gh_auth_token(account) helper running `gh auth token [--user <account>]`. github_token still wins; gh is only invoked when gh_account is set or gh_token_fallback is true, keeping existing public-repo behaviour and tests deterministic.
3. Builder helpers with_github_token/with_gh_account/with_gh_token_fallback and resolved_token().
4. Tests: auth header present on downloads when token set; auth stripped on cross-host redirect; resolved_token prefers explicit token without invoking gh.
5. README docs for private-repo + gh-account configuration.

Filed from updatable-cli dev session on operator request.

title: Add a compile-checked rustdoc example (doc-test) for the primary current_status path
description:
The crate currently has 0 doc-tests (cargo test reports "Doc-tests updatable_cli: running 0 tests"). The README usage examples are not compile-checked (the README is not wired in via doc(include_str!), and its runnable-looking blocks would hit the network), so the documented public-API usage can silently rot as the API evolves.

Add a single hermetic, network-free crate-level rustdoc example (a real runnable doc-test) to the module-level docs in src/lib.rs that exercises the primary status path:
- construct UpdaterConfig::new(tool, version, repo)
- set config.install_dir = Some(<temp path>) so the example never touches a real install dir
- call Updater::new(config).current_status()? and assert on tool/current_version and the derived installed/next paths

current_status performs no network or filesystem writes (only path computation + .exists() stats), so the doc-test is deterministic and fast. Use the `# Ok::<(), anyhow::Error>(())` trailing pattern (same as the README) so `?` works.

Acceptance: `cargo test` now runs >=1 doc-test and it passes; fmt + clippy + the existing 22 unit tests stay green. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: check_latest: friendlier errors for no-releases (404) and rate-limit (403/429)
description:
check_latest() in src/lib.rs propagates raw ureq errors instead of giving actionable messages for the two most common failure modes when polling GitHub releases:

- 404: the repo has no published releases yet (very common for a freshly set-up tool). Currently surfaces as a generic `GET <url>` ureq Status error.
- 403/429: GitHub API rate limiting (anonymous requests are limited to ~60/hr). Currently surfaces as a generic Status error with no hint that adding a token would fix it.

This is inconsistent with download_bytes(), which already maps `ureq::Error::Status(code, _)` to a clear `GET <url> returned HTTP <code>` message.

Fix: in check_latest, match on `request.call()`:
- 404 -> bail with "no published GitHub releases for <repo_slug> yet (GET <url> returned 404)"
- 403 | 429 -> bail with a message noting the request was rate-limited/forbidden and suggesting `UpdaterConfig::with_github_token` / `with_gh_token_fallback` to raise the limit
- other Status(code) -> "GET <url> returned HTTP <code>" (consistent with download_bytes)
- transport Err -> "GET <url>: <err>"

Add tests using a small std-only mock-HTTP helper that returns a custom status line (extend spawn_one_shot_http): one asserting the friendly no-releases message on 404, one asserting the rate-limit/token hint on 403.

Acceptance: cargo test/clippy/fmt pass; new tests cover 404 + 403 paths; behaviour unchanged on the success path. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: [broken-on-main] Windows CI wrongly requires untracked Cargo.lock
description: The native Windows job introduced by bd-3250c4 reaches the x86_64-pc-windows-msvc test step, then fails because the library intentionally does not track Cargo.lock while the workflow invokes cargo test --locked. GitHub run 29237950144, job 86776950926: cannot create Cargo.lock because --locked was passed. Remove --locked from both Windows test commands, validate workflow and native/cross compilation, land immediately, and confirm a fresh Windows job proceeds past dependency resolution. Discovered during post-land monitoring of bd-3250c4.

title: Install a downloaded release to an explicit target directory
description: Today the updater only replaces the currently running executable in place, so consumers have no first-party option when the running binary is immutable or package-managed (for example a /nix/store caravan binary), where an in-place write is impossible and would corrupt the store closure if it somehow succeeded. Add a generic capability: resolve and download the selected release asset, verify its digest, and install it to an explicit caller-supplied target directory instead of over the current executable, preserving version resolution, asset selection, digest verification, executable permissions, and atomic replace within that directory. Deliberate scope boundary: this crate must NOT decide where installing is acceptable - no package-manager detection, no PATH-precedence policy, no store protection. It takes an explicit destination and reports exactly what it wrote: resolved source asset, version, destination path, artifact hash. Callers own policy. Consumer counterpart is a Caravan bead adding the forced self-update path, which refuses store and Homebrew destinations, requires the destination to precede the package-managed binary in PATH, and emits a loud shadowing receipt.

title: Post-stage self-test: verify staged binary runs before promoting
description: Idea (drafted while idle): before promoting a staged binary, run it as a quick health check (e.g. <tool>_next --version) and only promote if it executes cleanly. Catches arch/ABI mismatches, corrupt downloads, and missing dynamic deps before they replace the working binary. Cheap, network-free, big safety win for run_update. Configurable command/timeout via UpdaterConfig.

title: Move CI to self-hosted azure-ephemeral runners (runs-on tag)
description:
Operator directive (2026-06-28): bring CI onto the new self-hosted azure-ephemeral GitHub runners. One agent per project adds the runner tag to all that project's CI; updatable-cli has a single agent (this one), so it owns the updatable-cli change.

Change .github/workflows/ci.yml job(s) from `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` to `runs-on: [self-hosted, azure-ephemeral]` (x86 Linux self-hosted runners). updatable-cli is Unix-only and its CI is a single Linux fmt+clippy+test job, so x86 azure-ephemeral is sufficient.
